trap: English 'dream of' often triggers the incorrect preposition 'de'.
example_es: Anoche soñé con vivir junto al mar.
example_en: Last night I dreamt of living by the sea.

trap: English 'depend on' may lead learners to use the incorrect 'en'.
example_es: El éxito depende de que todos colaboremos.
example_en: Success depends on all of us working together.

en: to trust or have confidence in
trap: Do not use 'de' or omit the preposition before the object of trust.
example_es: Confío en que llegarás a tiempo.
example_en: I trust that you'll arrive on time.

trap: The English construction 'consist of' often produces the incorrect calque 'consistir de'.
example_es: El trabajo consiste en revisar los datos.
example_en: The job consists of reviewing the data.

trap: Unlike English 'marry someone', Spanish requires 'con' after 'casarse'.
example_es: Se casó con su pareja el año pasado.
example_en: She married her partner last year.

trap: English 'with' may prompt the incorrect 'con'; Spanish uses 'de'.
example_es: Se enamoró de un compañero de trabajo.
example_en: She fell in love with a coworker.

trap: Do not treat pronominal 'acordarse' like transitive 'recordar'; it requires 'de'.
example_es: Acuérdate de cerrar la ventana.
example_en: Remember to close the window.

trap: Pronominal 'olvidarse' requires 'de', whereas non-pronominal 'olvidar' takes a direct object.
example_es: Me olvidé de comprar pan.
example_en: I forgot to buy bread.

trap: For 'try to', use 'tratar de', not 'tratar a' or 'tratar en'.
example_es: Trato de dormir ocho horas cada noche.
example_en: I try to sleep eight hours every night.

trap: Use 'dejar de' for ceasing an activity; 'dejar para' means postponing it.
example_es: Dejó de fumar hace dos años.
example_en: He stopped smoking two years ago.

trap: The recent-past construction uses 'de', not 'a'.
example_es: Acabo de hablar con la directora.
example_en: I've just spoken to the headteacher.

trap: Spanish uses 'a' before the following infinitive, not 'de'.
example_es: Empezó a llover justo cuando salíamos.
example_en: It started raining just as we were leaving.

trap: Unlike English, Spanish inserts 'a' before the infinitive.
example_es: Aprendí a conducir en Zaragoza.
example_en: I learnt to drive in Zaragoza.

trap: English often omits 'to', but Spanish normally requires 'a' before the infinitive.
example_es: ¿Me ayudas a mover este armario?
example_en: Will you help me move this wardrobe?

trap: Do not omit 'a' before the action being refused.
example_es: Se negó a firmar el contrato.
example_en: He refused to sign the contract.

trap: The action after 'atreverse' is introduced by 'a', not 'de'.
example_es: No me atrevo a decírselo.
example_en: I don't dare tell him.

trap: English 'insist on' corresponds to 'en', not 'sobre' or 'a'.
example_es: Insistió en pagar él la cena.
example_en: He insisted on paying for dinner himself.

trap: Use 'pensar en' for the object of thought; 'pensar de' asks for an opinion.
example_es: Pienso mucho en mis abuelos.
example_en: I think about my grandparents a lot.

trap: English 'count on' does not translate with 'en'; Spanish uses 'con'.
example_es: Contamos con vosotros para terminar hoy.
example_en: We're counting on you all to finish today.

trap: Use 'por' for the cause of worry; 'preocuparse de' more often means taking care to do something.
example_es: Se preocupa demasiado por lo que piensen los demás.
example_en: She worries too much about what other people might think.

trap: Use 'por' for a goal or cause, not 'para'.
example_es: Luchamos por conservar el cine del barrio.
example_en: We're fighting to preserve the neighbourhood cinema.

trap: Use 'optar por' for choosing; 'optar a' means competing or applying for something.
example_es: Optaron por aplazar la reunión.
example_en: They chose to postpone the meeting.

trap: English 'lack' is transitive, but Spanish 'carecer' requires 'de'.
example_es: El informe carece de datos que respalden la conclusión.
example_en: The report lacks data supporting the conclusion.

trap: Use 'constar de' for components; 'constar en' means being recorded somewhere.
example_es: El curso consta de seis módulos.
example_en: The course consists of six modules.

trap: English 'laugh at' may trigger the incorrect 'a'; Spanish uses 'de'.
example_es: Se burlaron de su acento durante la cena.
example_en: They made fun of his accent during dinner.

trap: The cause of regret is introduced by 'de', not 'por'.
example_es: Me arrepiento de no haber aceptado la oferta.
example_en: I regret not having accepted the offer.

trap: English 'about' often prompts 'sobre', but the standard regime is 'quejarse de'.
example_es: Los vecinos se quejaron del ruido nocturno.
example_en: The neighbours complained about the noise at night.

trap: Do not omit 'de', including before a clause introduced by 'que'.
example_es: Me di cuenta de que había dejado las llaves en casa.
example_en: I realised that I had left my keys at home.

en: to feel like; look forward to
trap: The desired activity follows 'ganas de', not 'ganas para'.
example_es: Tengo ganas de verte este fin de semana.
example_en: I'm looking forward to seeing you this weekend.

en: to be about to do something
trap: The fixed expression ends in 'de', not 'para'.
example_es: El tren está a punto de salir.
example_en: The train is about to leave.

en: to take care of; deal with
trap: The matter or task handled follows 'de', not 'en'.
example_es: Yo me ocupo de preparar el presupuesto mensual.
example_en: I take care of preparing the monthly budget.

trap: Do not use 'por' after 'encargarse'; responsibility is introduced by 'de'.
example_es: Laura se encarga de reservar el alojamiento.
example_en: Laura is responsible for booking the accommodation.

trap: The thing omitted is introduced by 'de', despite English 'without'.
example_es: Podemos prescindir del coche porque el metro está cerca.
example_en: We can do without the car because the underground is nearby.

trap: In the sense of having something available, 'disponer' requires 'de'.
example_es: Disponemos de tres salas de reuniones.
example_en: We have three meeting rooms available.

trap: Use 'de' for what makes you glad; 'alegrarse por alguien' expresses happiness on that person's behalf.
example_es: Me alegro de que hayas venido.
example_en: I'm glad you came.

trap: Do not use 'sobre' directly after 'enterarse'; the governed preposition is 'de'.
example_es: Me enteré del cambio por una compañera.
example_en: I found out about the change through a colleague.

en: to convince someone of or to do something
trap: After the person convinced, the argument or action is introduced by 'de', not 'a'.
example_es: Convencí a Marta de que pidiera una segunda opinión.
example_en: I convinced Marta to seek a second opinion.

en: to devote oneself to; work in
trap: The occupation or activity follows 'a', not 'en'.
example_es: Mi hermano se dedica a diseñar páginas web.
example_en: My brother works designing websites.

trap: English 'used to' can obscure that Spanish always requires 'a' here.
example_es: Me he acostumbrado a trabajar desde casa.
example_en: I've got used to working from home.

trap: English 'renounce' or 'give up' has no equivalent preposition, but Spanish requires 'a'.
example_es: Renunció al puesto por motivos personales.
example_en: She resigned from the position for personal reasons.

en: to agree to; gain access to
trap: Whether it means agreeing or gaining access, the complement follows 'a'.
example_es: La empresa accedió a devolvernos el dinero.
example_en: The company agreed to refund our money.

trap: English 'attend' is transitive, but Spanish 'asistir' requires 'a'.
example_es: Mañana asistiré a una reunión en Madrid.
example_en: Tomorrow I'll attend a meeting in Madrid.

trap: Do not translate English 'belong to' with 'de'; Spanish uses 'a'.
example_es: Este archivo pertenece al departamento jurídico.
example_en: This file belongs to the legal department.

trap: The object referred to follows 'a', not 'sobre'.
example_es: El artículo se refiere a un estudio reciente.
example_en: The article refers to a recent study.

trap: English 'oppose' is transitive, but Spanish 'oponerse' requires 'a'.
example_es: Muchos vecinos se oponen a construir otro aparcamiento.
example_en: Many residents oppose building another car park.

trap: English 'contribute to' corresponds to 'a', not 'para'.
example_es: Esta medida contribuirá a reducir el consumo de energía.
example_en: This measure will help reduce energy consumption.

trap: The following infinitive requires 'a', just as in the fixed construction 'tender a'.
example_es: Cuando está cansado, tiende a cometer más errores.
example_en: When he's tired, he tends to make more mistakes.

en: to play a game or sport
trap: In European Spanish, games and sports follow 'a'; 'jugar con' means playing with someone or something.
example_es: Los niños juegan al fútbol en el parque.
example_en: The children play football in the park.

trap: The focus of attention follows 'en', not 'a'.
example_es: Fíjate en cómo cambia la luz al atardecer.
example_en: Notice how the light changes at sunset.

trap: English 'focus on' maps to 'centrarse en', not 'centrarse sobre'.
example_es: El debate se centró en buscar soluciones prácticas.
example_en: The debate focused on finding practical solutions.

trap: The basis is introduced by 'en', not 'sobre'.
example_es: La película se basa en una novela histórica.
example_en: The film is based on a historical novel.

en: to take time to do something
trap: Spanish inserts 'en' before the action, unlike English 'take time to'.
example_es: Tardamos dos horas en llegar a Toledo.
example_en: It took us two hours to reach Toledo.

trap: Use 'en' for the resulting state, not 'a' or 'de'.
example_es: El antiguo almacén se convirtió en una biblioteca.
example_en: The old warehouse became a library.

trap: English 'influence' is transitive, but Spanish normally uses 'influir en'.
example_es: La luz influye en nuestro estado de ánimo.
example_en: Light influences our mood.

trap: Agreement with a person or view uses 'con', not 'a'.
example_es: Coincido contigo en lo esencial.
example_en: I agree with you on the essentials.

en: to settle for; be satisfied with
trap: The accepted result follows 'con', not 'de'.
example_es: No me conformo con una explicación tan vaga.
example_en: I won't settle for such a vague explanation.

trap: The item something is mistaken for is introduced by 'con', not 'por'.
example_es: No confundas la cortesía con la amistad.
example_en: Don't confuse politeness with friendship.

trap: Use 'por' for the person or subject sought; 'preguntar a' introduces the person being asked.
example_es: En recepción pregunté por Ana.
example_en: I asked for Ana at reception.

en: to be useful for; serve to
trap: Use 'para' for purpose; 'servir de' means serving as something.
example_es: Este botón sirve para apagar la pantalla.
example_en: This button is used to switch off the screen.

trap: Use 'contra' for an opponent or harmful force; 'luchar por' introduces the goal or cause defended.
example_es: Los médicos luchan contra la propagación del virus.
example_en: Doctors are fighting against the spread of the virus.
